metadata.title: TSMC Customers Face Bigger Chip Costs

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE:TSM) reportedly plans to raise chipmaking prices by 5% to 10% in 2027, giving the world's largest contract chipmaker another lever to protect margins as production costs rise.
According to Nikkei Asia, customers including Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL), Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) and AMD (NASDAQ:AMD) have been informed of the planned increases. Orders for high-performance computing chips above original forecasts could carry an additional 10% to 15% premium, pushing total hikes even higher for some advanced products.
-

TSMC manufactures chips designed by many of the world's largest technology companies. Its pricing power comes from its leadership in advanced manufacturing, where customers have few alternatives for cutting-edge AI and smartphone processors.
The company also plans increases of up to 10% for mature-node chips, which accounted for roughly 23% of recent quarterly revenue. Higher material, equipment and overseas fab costs are driving the move.
